findings.reason: The first implementation compared selection_sha256 directly and produced selection_mismatch whenever a selected file changed size. The test fixture now covers a normal size change, and selection identity is checked by query terms plus selected path set; a changed frozen tree gets its own tree_mismatch omission.

The first draft treated text:null as a legitimate partial snapshot. The real snapshot producer always includes decoded text and hashes it, so a null or non-string text is now invalid_snapshot rather than a fabricated coverage state.

The first validator did not verify tree_schema, per-row selection_size_changed against selection_bytes/bytes, aggregate size-change counts, or total_bytes against max_bytes. Tests and implementation now refuse these contradictions.

The early budget loop could rewrite max_files/max_bytes or loop on report_bytes insertion. The final implementation budgets the complete public envelope, reports content bytes excluding report_bytes/report_sha256, converges by dropping entries/detail, refuses only budgets below the minimal envelope, and has a 1..511-byte boundary test.
The file limit initially exposed only a count. It now emits bounded omitted_paths in sorted order; if byte pressure removes that detail, the max_bytes omission remains.
compared_files now counts changed paths represented before limits, and added/deleted rows use text_compared=false because there is no two-sided text comparison.

A separate read-only Codex reviewer was started against the five-path diff. It produced no verdict after more than two minutes and was interrupted; author-side review and tests are not rewritten as independent review. This is a known review limitation, not a pass.
